name: Barnard's Star
kind: The fastest-moving star in the sky
blurb: A small red star just 6 light-years away. It crosses the sky faster than any other star: about 10 arcseconds every year.

name: Epsilon Indi B
kind: A pair of brown dwarfs orbiting a star
blurb: Two brown dwarfs, too small to shine like stars, circling the star Epsilon Indi 12 light-years away. SPHEREx sees the pair as one dot.
source: Gaia DR3 6412596012146801152 (the pair is unresolved by SPHEREx)

name: WISE 0855
blurb: Colder than ice and only 7 light-years away. It is invisible in SPHEREx's shorter wavelengths and appears only near 4 microns.
source: AllWISE J085510.74-071442.5 position (mean epoch 2010.6); proper motion and parallax from Luhman & Esplin 2016, AJ 152, 78, Table 4

name: RW Aurigae
kind: A young star that changes brightness
blurb: A young star still gathering material from a surrounding disk. It does not move measurably, but its brightness changes.

name: R Draconis
blurb: A giant star that swells and shrinks over about 8 months, changing brightness as it does. It is so bright that it saturates SPHEREx.
